problem: Suppose $C$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and $det(C)=-5,$ What is the value of $det(4C)?$

feedback.problem: Suppose $Y$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $det(Y)=-3.$ What is the value of $det(4Y)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot Y)={k}^{n}\cdot det(Y).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=4$ and $n=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(4Y) & ={4}^{3}\cdot det(Y) \\  & =64\cdot (-3) \\  & =-192.\end{aligned}
$$
